work.title: The problem, what I built, what changed.

maslinescu.title: Măslinescu® — an olive-oil shop with its own ops room
maslinescu.problem: A growing store where a silent PHP error or a blocked order email means lost sales — and nobody finds out until a customer calls.
maslinescu.built: Six custom plugins — a tiered loyalty club that also counts in-store purchases through a cash-register API, photo & video reviews, customer restrictions, gift messages — plus a Grafana + Loki + Prometheus stack with Slack alerts.
maslinescu.result: Problems surface in Slack first, and mail-blacklist issues are caught by monitoring, not by complaints. Every plugin ships through PHPStan, tests and an automated deploy. Next up: an AI shopping assistant.

tablouri.title: TablouriColorate — a product configurator customers actually finish
tablouri.problem: After moving to WooCommerce, the canvas-print shop needed far richer product options. The jQuery version crawled during photo uploads, and the React rewrite that followed shipped 520–730 KB of JavaScript per page.
tablouri.built: One dependency-free configurator for six product types — canvas, multicanvas, collage, poster, banner and sticker — with crop previews drawn on canvas, prices computed on the server and hardened uploads.
tablouri.result: About 12 KB gzipped instead of 520–730 KB per page, one price formula shared by browser and server, and a new product that splits one photo across up to 12 canvases. On a maintenance plan since 2018.

lumea.title: Lumea BookTruck — volunteers upload from the field, no accounts needed
lumea.problem: The BookTruck mobile library of Cărțile pe Față lends books to children in rural schools — and every trip leaves hundreds of photos scattered across volunteers' phones and WhatsApp groups.
lumea.built: A Next.js + Prisma + Better Auth panel for the catalogue, stock and loans (with ISBN scanning in the browser), plus one-link upload sessions that send files straight to the NGO's Google Drive in resumable chunks.
lumea.result: One link per trip, files land organised in Drive, and large uploads never pass through — or overload — the server. Librarians and volunteers share one panel with role-based permissions.
